question: What is the primary function of the large intestine during digestion?

options.B: Absorbing water and salts from waste
options.C: Initiating the chemical digestion of food
options.D: Breaking down fats into fatty acids

explanation: The large intestine mainly acts to pull water and essential salts back into the body, turning liquid waste into formed stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which muscle action is responsible for moving waste along the colon?
explanation: Peristalsis refers to the wave-like muscular contractions that push food and waste steadily through the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which medication class is widely known to cause constipation as a side effect?
explanation: Opioids slow down gastrointestinal motility significantly, which frequently leads to stubborn constipation in patients taking them. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h2)

question: A patient's waste moves through the colon at a normal speed, but they still struggle with hard stools and straining because of their diet. What do we call this type of constipation?
explanation: Even when the gut moves at a normal speed, everyday things like not eating enough fiber or drinking less water can cause normal-transit constipation. Easy peasy once you break it down!

question: What is a fecal impaction?

options.A: A hard mass of stool stuck in the rectum
options.B: An infection of the large intestine lining
options.C: The complete absence of bowel sounds
options.D: A tear in the external anal sphincter

explanation: Fecal impaction happens when dried stool collects and packs tightly in the rectum, blocking normal passage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why does chronic straining often lead to the development of hemorrhoids?

options.A: It increases pressure on the blood vessels around the anus
options.B: It strips the protective mucous layer off the colon
options.C: It stops the liver from filtering blood properly
options.D: It causes rapid dehydration of the entire body

explanation: Straining forces extra blood into the rectal and anal veins, causing them to swell and form hemorrhoids. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h3)

question: In what order should you assess a patient's abdomen during a physical exam?
explanation: Always listen (auscultate) before you press (palpate)! If you press first, you might push things around and change the natural bowel sounds. Smart nursing practice!

question: An elderly patient leaks small amounts of liquid stool daily. What should the nurse suspect first?
explanation: Liquid stool often leaks around a hard, impacted blockage in the rectum, which can trick people into thinking it is diarrhea. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h4)

question: How do bulk-forming laxatives primarily work to relieve constipation?

options.A: By absorbing water to increase stool size and softness
options.B: By directly irritating the colon wall to force contractions
options.C: By killing bacteria that dry out the stool
options.D: By coating the rectum with oil for easy passage

explanation: Bulk-forming agents swell up by drawing in water, which creates a larger, softer stool that triggers stretch receptors in the bowel. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why must patients taking bulk-forming laxatives drink plenty of water with them?

options.A: To activate the chemical formula in the liver first
options.B: To stop the kidneys from producing too much urine
options.C: To prevent the drug from absorbing into the bloodstream
options.D: To prevent the supplement from swelling and blocking the throat or bowel

explanation: Without enough water, bulk-forming agents can absorb moisture from the esophagus or intestines and cause a dangerous blockage. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is the time right after breakfast often the best time to try having a bowel movement?

options.A: Stomach acid levels are at their lowest point of the day
options.B: Blood pressure peaks and helps push waste forward
options.C: Eating food triggers a natural wave of activity in the colon
options.D: Digestive enzymes are most active in the rectum then

explanation: Eating stimulates the gastrocolic reflex, which increases muscle contractions in the colon and creates a natural urge to go. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which nursing action is best for preventing constipation in an immobile bedbound patient?

options.A: Administering a strong daily enema before breakfast
options.B: Encouraging fluids, high-fiber foods, and passive or active movement
options.C: Telling the patient to hold bowel movements until evening
options.D: Restricting fluid intake to slow down digestion

explanation: Combining hydration, fiber, and physical movement addresses the main lifestyle causes of constipation safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h6)
